We now explain how to obtain the threshold k ∼N 2(1−a)/3 for a ∈[0, 1). We do not present the
mathematical details for brevity, but just explain the general strategy. We separate the argument into two
parts: we first show that the eigenvalues corresponding to indices i ∼N a are (asymptotically) independent
for k ≫N 2(1−a)/3 and then that they are strongly correlated for k ≪N 2(1−a)/3.
For k ≫N 2(1−a)/3, we follow a strategy similar to Section 3, i.e. we show the independence of the
eigenvalues using a Dyson Brownian motion (DBM) argument. More precisely, we couple the time evo-
